name: Red Dwarf: Three Million Years Late
author: Vaster Than Life team (unofficial fan campaign)

campaign.title: Red Dwarf: Three Million Years Late
campaign.blurb: Unofficial fan campaign. Red Dwarf has been towed away by Simulants. The last human alive, a hologram, a cat and a mechanoid chase it across deep space in a mining shuttle, with Holly on the backup line. Its own ships, guns, skutters, GELFs, Simulants and about forty years' worth of bad luck. Red Dwarf belongs to its creators.
campaign.intro: Holly's face fills the shuttle's screen, looking as if she has just been woken up. "Bit of news. Red Dwarf's gone. A Simulant battle group hooked a tow line on her while you lot were asleep, and they're dragging her off to their Death Ship to strip her for parts. I'm still aboard, sort of, on the emergency backup. You'll want to follow the tow beacon. Eight sectors. Probably. I've rounded down."
campaign.giftLine: "Kryten has packed a few things for the trip. You can take one. He'll be inconsolable about the rest."
bossLines: The Death Ship's commander appears on screen, all chrome and contempt. "Organics. In a shuttle. Chasing a battle group. I shall enjoy cataloguing your remains."
"You again. I have upgraded my hatred of you. It is now military grade."
"Every gun. Every drone. Every last ounce of spite. FIRE."
chatter: Lister: Anyone seen the last poppadom? It was right here. It had a name.
Rimmer: I'd like it noted in the log that I was right. About everything. Generally.
Cat: Hold on. I need to check my hair before we jump. Okay. Perfect. Again.
Kryten: I've ironed the emergency blankets, sir. And the emergency. It was creased.
Holly: I've been thinking. Then I stopped. It's quieter.
Lister: Three million years from Earth and the vending machine still eats my coins.
Rimmer: I've drawn up a rota for the rota. It's colour-coded. Nobody's read it.
Cat: Something smells funny. Oh. It's Lister.
Holly: I've worked out how far we've come. Then I forgot. So, about the same.
Kryten: The Simulants are gaining, sirs. I've prepared a lovely trifle, just in case it's our last.
Lister: Has anyone seen my other sock? Not that one. The one that moves.
Rimmer: When we get Red Dwarf back I'll want it noted that I was in command. Technically. In my head.
Cat: Every time we jump, I look even better. Coincidence? I don't think so.
Kryten: I've reorganised the cargo hold by smell, sir. You won't like the end with the curry.
Holly: There's an emergency. Hang on. No, there isn't. Carry on.
Lister: If we live, I'm going to have the biggest curry in history. If we don't, also curry.
Skutter has painted a rude word on the hull. Kryten is pretending not to know which one.
The food dispenser has produced a cup of soup with a fork in it. Again.
Kryten: The bazookoids are tracking beautifully, sir. They've already found three of your socks.
Lister: The cannon's getting warm. That's either good or very bad.
Rimmer's Scattergun has hit the target, the scenery and, briefly, Rimmer.
The toaster lobber has fired another crumpet. The crew ate it.
Lister: I've found a guitar string. Not a guitar. Just the string. It's a start.
Rimmer: I've written my memoirs. Chapter one is called Being Right. Chapter two is also called Being Right.
Cat: I've decided my new look is 'heroic'. You can tell because of the cape.
Kryten: Sirs, I have made a laminated card of what to do in an emergency. Step one: don't eat the laminated card, Mr Lister.
Holly: I've noticed the stars are moving. Or we are. One of the two.
Lister: Holly, how far to Red Dwarf? ... Holly? ... She's asleep again.
Rimmer: When the Simulants catch us, I'll be negotiating. From the back. Behind the Cat.
Cat: Never jump on an empty stomach. Or a full one. Jump on someone else's.
Kryten: I've reorganised the spice rack by danger level, sirs. Mr Lister's vindaloo powder needed its own shelf. And a lock.
A skutter has fallen in love with the mop. The mop has not been consulted.
Holly: Bit of good news. The engines are fine. Bit of bad news. I don't know what the engines are.
Lister: If anyone sees my lucky can of beans, don't open it. It's lucky because it's never been opened.
Rimmer: I've put in a request for a bigger bunk. I'm a hologram. I don't use the bunk. It's the principle.
Cat: Kryten, is this jacket too much? ... Correct answer: it isn't enough.
Kryten: The toilet is making a noise again, sirs. I've given it a name to keep my spirits up.
The scanner picks up a Simulant distress call. It is a recording of someone laughing at you. It's quite well done.
Lister: I'm not saying the curry was off, but my spleen just filed for divorce.
Rimmer: Space Corps Directive 1742: no crew member shall touch the captain's biscuits. Yes, I wrote that one myself.
Cat: I don't need a mirror. Mirrors need me.
Kryten: I've ironed the socks, sir. And the toast. Habit, sir.
Holly: I've worked out where we are. It's here. You're welcome.
Lister: If I die out here, nobody's to look in my locker. Especially not the third shelf.
Rimmer: I'll have you know I was nearly a very important person. Twice.
Cat: Somebody's been wearing my cologne. It's me. It's always me.
Kryten: Sir, the toaster is asking if anyone would like a crumpet. Again. It's been asking for an hour.
Holly: The good news is the engines are fine. The bad news is the rest.

win.title: RED DWARF RECOVERED
win.text: The Death Ship breaks apart, and the tow line goes slack. Red Dwarf is yours again: battered, empty and three million years from anywhere. Lister puts the kettle on. Rimmer starts writing a report about his own heroism. The Cat finds a new mirror. Kryten starts on the washing up. Holly says something nobody quite follows. Earth is still a very long way off.

campaign.lose: Starbug drifts, silent. Somewhere far ahead, Red Dwarf keeps going without them, and Holly counts the stars for company.

races.name: Hologram
races.desc: Made of light. Fire and vacuum can't touch him. Neither can a spanner, or a punch, very well. Simulant hard-light disruptors scramble them.

races.name: Felis sapiens
races.desc: Evolved from house cats. Very fast, very good in a fight, and very busy looking at himself.

races.name: Mechanoid
races.desc: A service mechanoid. Repairs anything, needs no air, and apologises for both.

races.name: GELF
races.desc: A Genetically Engineered Life Form. Built to work, decided against it. Strong, grumpy and loyal to anyone who brings snacks.

races.name: Simulant
races.desc: A combat android that hates everything organic, and most things that aren't.

races.name: Agonoid
races.desc: A battle droid that went feral. Mostly spare parts and grudges.

races.name: Waxdroid
races.desc: A theme-park robot dressed as somebody famous. Fights for its side of a war nobody else remembers.

ships.name: Starbug 1
ships.desc: A battered three-bulb mining shuttle. Its twin cannon warms up as it fires, and its bazookoids never miss. It smells of curry.

ships.name: Blue Midget
ships.desc: Starbug's smaller, bluer cousin. Its mining laser salvages scrap from every hit, and its toaster feeds the crew.

ships.name: Starbug Mk III
ships.desc: Three crashed Starbugs welded into one by a skutter with ambition. More hull, more guns, and the toilet is on the outside.

ships.name: Holoship Smug Glow
ships.desc: Made of light and arrogance. Fast, well shielded, and its holograms can't burn or choke. The hull is mostly opinion.

ships.name: Captured GELF Canoe
ships.desc: Won in a wrestling match, a wedding and a misunderstanding. Bone, hide, a harpoon and boarders who love a scrap.

ships.name: Stolen Simulant Barge
ships.desc: Nicked while its Simulants were at a team-building day. Plasma lance, hacking, and a computer that asks politely to kill you.

ships.name: The Skutter Pram
ships.desc: Built by skutters from a laundry trolley and a fridge. Tiny, nippy, full of drones, and very sorry about all this.

sectors.name: Deep Space
sectors.blurb: Three million years from Earth and nothing for light years in every direction. Except trouble.
intro: Starbug's engines cough, then catch. The tow beacon blinks somewhere ahead. Lister puts his feet up on the console. Rimmer tells him to take them down.

sectors.name: GELF Territory
sectors.blurb: Genetically engineered lifeforms, all of them armed and most of them cross.
intro: Kryten warns that GELF tribes trade in everything, including visitors. The Cat checks his cufflinks, just in case.

sectors.name: Psi-Moon Belt
sectors.blurb: Moons that read your mind and reshape themselves to match it. Bring a calm mind. Or any mind.
intro: The moons here shift as you pass, turning into whatever whoever is on watch is thinking about. Right now, apparently, a giant curry.

sectors.name: Simulant Hunting Grounds
sectors.blurb: The battle group's own backyard. Heavy patrols, heavy guns, and no sense of humour.
intro: Simulant patrol codes crackle on every channel. Rimmer suggests hiding. Nobody can find a reason to disagree.

sectors.name: The Waxworks Drift
sectors.blurb: Abandoned theme-park planets, their wax droids still fighting a war nobody remembers starting.
intro: Old theme-park beacons still play their welcome jingles to nobody. Lister finds them oddly comforting. Rimmer finds them tacky.

sectors.name: The Backwards Reach
sectors.blurb: A region where time flows the wrong way. It ends well. Or begins well. Hard to say.
intro: The chronometer starts counting down instead of up. Kryten finds this deeply upsetting. Lister finds it means breakfast comes after dinner, and is delighted.

sectors.name: The Time Drift
sectors.blurb: Stasis leaks, white holes and echoes of things that haven't happened yet. Bring a watch. Bring two.
intro: Holly reports that time is a bit runny in this sector. The Cat is fine with it, provided it doesn't affect his hair.

sectors.name: The Garbage Trail
sectors.blurb: Three million years of Red Dwarf's rubbish, still drifting in a line across space. Some of it is valuable. Some of it is alive.
intro: Holly confirms it: every bin bag the ship ever jettisoned is out here. Lister recognises a sock.

sectors.name: The Mirror Sea
sectors.blurb: A stretch of space so still and polished that every ship sees itself coming. Some of the reflections fly better than you do.
intro: Holly reports that the stars ahead look exactly like the stars behind. Kryten checks. They are the stars behind. Rimmer combs his hair in the viewscreen and is pleased with both of him.

sectors.name: The Death Ship's Wake
sectors.blurb: Red Dwarf, on the end of a tow line, and the Death Ship dragging her towards the breakers.
intro: There she is: Red Dwarf, five miles of red metal, helpless on the end of a tow line. Ahead of her, the Death Ship. Holly's voice crackles through: "Oh good, you came. I was starting to talk to myself. Well. More."

events.text: Lister has found the last chicken vindaloo in the galley freezer, and is holding it like a holy relic. "It's the last one, man. The last curry in the universe." Everyone is looking at it.

choices.text: Share it out, one spoonful each.

effect.text: It is the best spoonful of food anyone has had in years. Even Kryten, who doesn't eat, has a little sniff. Morale soars.

choices.text: It's Lister's. Let him have it.

effect.text: Lister eats it slowly, with his eyes closed. He is unbearably cheerful for the rest of the sector.

choices.text: Freeze it again for an emergency.

effect.text: Kryten labels it EMERGENCY CURRY and puts it behind the reactor shielding. It will not be safe there. Nothing is safe from Lister.

events.text: Rimmer has found an automated exam station and is going to sit his astronavigation exam. Again. He has sat it more times than anyone can count, and failed it every time. He has brought a revision timetable. It is longer than the exam.

success.text: Against all known science, he passes. He frames the certificate and hangs it on the bridge, and is genuinely a better pilot for it.

fail.text: He panics, writes his name wrong, and faints. The exam station gives him a participation sticker. He wears it.

effect.text: Kryten sits it in a Rimmer mask and scores full marks. The station is suspicious. Rimmer is delighted, then furious, then delighted again.

choices.text: Keep flying. The tow beacon won't wait.

effect.text: Rimmer sulks for six jumps. It is very restful.

events.text: The Cat has found a moon of polished crystal, a perfect mirror half a mile wide, and he will not leave. "I have finally found something worthy of looking at me."

effect.text: He comes back glowing with confidence. In the next fight, nobody has ever dodged so stylishly.
The Cat is horrified, but the crystal sells beautifully.
He fights it all the way. He has never looked better doing it.

events.text: Kryten has something to confess. He has been running a hidden program for months: a list of everything he has ever done wrong. It is very long. Item one is ironing Lister's lucky socks.

effect.text: Kryten is so relieved he cleans the entire ship in one night, including several things that were meant to be dirty.

choices.text: Teach him to lie a little.

success.text: "The Simulants are... very handsome?" It's a start. He feels lighter, and so does the ship's software: he deletes a lot of nonsense along with the list.

fail.text: He tries to lie to the ship's computer, short-circuits, and spends a day thinking he is a toaster.

choices.text: Add your own items to the list.

effect.text: Kryten is overjoyed. A longer list means more to feel bad about. Some people are just built differently.

events.text: Holly comes through on the backup line. "I've worked out a shortcut. Straight through that black hole. I've done the maths. Twice. Got two different answers, so I averaged them."

success.text: You come out the other side half a sector ahead, slightly younger, and all wearing each other's socks.

fail.text: You come out the other side exactly where you went in, an hour later, and someone has been at the curry.

effect.text: Holly sulks. Holly sulking is mostly indistinguishable from Holly not sulking.
Rimmer recalculates for four hours and arrives at the same two answers. He averages them. You go round anyway.

events.text: The skutters, the little cleaning robots, have been busy. They have built an enormous model of Red Dwarf out of spare parts, mostly from the engines. They seem very proud.

choices.text: Admire it, then take the parts back.

effect.text: The skutters look crestfallen, but your engines work again.

choices.text: Let them keep it. It's a tribute.

effect.text: They follow everyone around for days, beeping happily. The crew feel very much at home.
The model turns out to be surprisingly well armed. It becomes your newest weapon.

events.text: Red Dwarf hangs on the tow line ahead, and the Death Ship ahead of her. Everyone looks at Lister. He looks at them. "Right. We go in, we cut her loose, we bring her home. Anyone got a better plan?"

effect.text: It isn't a plan, exactly, but everyone cheers anyway.
Page 211 turns out to be genuinely useful. Everyone else is mostly asleep by then.

choices.text: The Cat's plan: look good, win.

effect.text: It's not a bad plan. It has always worked for him.

events.text: A talking toaster is floating in space, broadcasting on every channel. "Would anybody like any toast? Muffins? A crumpet? I do a very nice bagel." It will not stop.

effect.text: It asks everyone if they want toast, every four minutes, forever. The crew are well fed and slowly going mad.

choices.text: Lister wants it for the galley.

effect.text: Lister and the toaster become best friends. Nobody else is allowed in the galley.
It asks if you'd like toast all the way down.

events.text: A GELF chieftain hails you. She has seen Lister on the long-range scanner and would like to marry him. Today. It is a great honour. Refusing is a great insult, and insults are settled with harpoons.

choices.text: Lister says yes, then you run.

success.text: The wedding is lovely. The escape is better. Lister keeps the wedding gifts.

fail.text: She notices you running. Harpoons follow.

effect.text: She takes one look at Rimmer and laughs for eleven minutes. You use the time to leave.

success.text: Kryten talks her into a trade deal instead. Everyone is relieved, except possibly Lister.

fail.text: Kryten apologises so much that she declares war on politeness.

events.text: Something has crept aboard: a shape-shifter that feeds on emotions.

choices.text: Find out what it has eaten.

events.text: A psi-moon has locked onto the ship and is reshaping itself around whoever is on watch. It is Rimmer. The moon is now a swamp of self-doubt, with a bog of regret.

effect.text: The moon becomes a gigantic, flattering mirror. The Cat finds a fortune in reflective crystal while he admires himself.

choices.text: Fight your way through Rimmer's mind.

success.text: You find his self-confidence, tiny and hiding behind a filing cabinet. He is briefly bearable.

fail.text: The bog of regret claims a hull plate.

effect.text: The moon waves you off, looking hurt.

events.text: A planet where time runs backwards. A bar there will pay you to un-drink their drinks, and the local hospital is full of people getting worse.

effect.text: You end the shift sober and richer than you started.
Your hull slowly un-dents as you sit in orbit.

choices.text: Leave before you un-meet each other.

effect.text: Wise. Kryten had already started un-cleaning.

events.text: A derelict station's vending machine has developed a personality, and the personality is rude. It will dispense missiles, but only to people it likes.

success.text: It likes Lister. Everybody's machines like Lister. It hands over a whole rack.

fail.text: It calls Lister several very rude names and keeps his money.

effect.text: A polite vending machine is a generous one.
It shouts after you for a long time.

events.text: A theme park planet where wax droids of history's heroes and villains are still at war. Both sides want to recruit you. Both sides have a lot of guns.

success.text: You help win a battle that has run for centuries. The grateful heroes give you their armoury.

fail.text: The heroes turn out to be terrible at war. You barely get out.

choices.text: Melt the lot and sell the wax.

effect.text: Very profitable. Slightly upsetting.
Distant wax cannons boom as you leave.

events.text: "Organic vermin. You will surrender the vessel and submit to cataloguing." The Simulant sounds almost bored.

choices.text: Rimmer surrenders first, on everyone's behalf.

success.text: The Simulant is so disgusted by Rimmer's grovelling that it leaves.

fail.text: "Pathetic." The guns warm up anyway.

events.text: "Your life signs are pitiful. Your ship is pitiful. Your hair, organic, is pitiful." The Cat is very offended.

effect.text: The Cat answers with a lot of guns.

events.text: A GELF war canoe pulls alongside. Its crew bangs on the hull, which is how GELFs say hello. Or goodbye. It is hard to tell.

success.text: They are delighted. Curry is very rare out here. They leave you alone, and a little richer.

fail.text: They eat it, and then attack anyway, now with more energy.

events.text: {crew} has found a headset in a derelict, labelled "Better Than Life: the total-immersion game". Inside the game, everyone gets everything they have ever wanted. Nobody who plays it ever wants to take it off. {crew} is already holding it a bit close to their face.

choices.text: Have a quick go. Just one.

success.text: Everyone has a lovely time and, astonishingly, everyone takes the headset off afterwards. The crew are rested and happier than they've been in months.

fail.text: Two days later Kryten finds the crew sitting in a circle, smiling at nothing, very hungry. The Simulants have gained a lot of ground.

effect.text: It goes out of the airlock in pieces. {crew} watches it go with the look of somebody waving off a holiday.

choices.text: Let Kryten play it. He can't enjoy anything.

effect.text: Kryten spends an hour in paradise, which for him is ironing a never-ending pile of shirts. He comes out refreshed and finds the game's prize vault on the way.

events.text: A droid in a long dark cloak steps out of a time hole onto your bridge. "I am the Inquisitor. I travel through all of time, judging whether each life has been worth living. Those found wanting are erased, and replaced by someone who would have done better." It looks at {crew}. It does not look impressed.

success.text: You make a stirring speech about doing your best. The Inquisitor considers it, then lowers its weapon. "Barely. But yes." It vanishes, and leaves behind a strange feeling of having been told off by the universe.

fail.text: "Insufficient," it says, and opens fire. Your crew are going to have to argue with their fists.

afterWin.text: Among the wreck is the Inquisitor's time gauntlet. Kryten says it's best not to think about it too hard, and sells it.

success.text: Rimmer talks for two hours about his achievements. The Inquisitor leaves out of sheer boredom.

fail.text: Halfway through Rimmer's list of achievements, the Inquisitor attacks.

afterWin.text: You pick through the wreck. Rimmer insists he won the argument.

choices.text: Fight it now, before it decides.

effect.text: Nothing gets erased if you hit it first.

afterWin.text: The Inquisitor's ship crumples into a time hole of its own. It drops its tools on the way out.

events.text: A battered test ship drops out of a dimension rip in front of you, and out of it climbs a dashing, confident pilot with Rimmer's face and none of Rimmer's personality. Ace, the hero from another dimension, needs fuel to jump on to the next universe that needs saving. The real Rimmer has gone a funny colour.

effect.text: Ace thanks everyone by name, kisses Kryten on the head and gives you his spare cannon. Then he's gone in a flash of light. The crew stare at the real Rimmer for a long time.

choices.text: Ask him to train the crew.

effect.text: Ace drills everyone for an afternoon, cheerfully and brilliantly. Even Rimmer improves, out of spite.

choices.text: Let Rimmer talk to him alone.

effect.text: Nobody knows what they said. Rimmer comes back quiet, and for one whole sector he is almost brave.

events.text: An ocean moon, very still. Holly picks up a creature beneath its surface the size of a city. Kryten checks the records: a despair squid, whose ink makes anyone nearby believe their whole life has been a failure. There is a wrecked survey ship on the seabed, full of salvage.

success.text: The crew keep their eyes shut, hum loudly and think about curry. It works. The survey ship had a full equipment locker.

fail.text: The ink gets in. For a day everyone sits around listing their failures out loud. Rimmer's list takes most of it. Nobody is hurt, exactly, but nobody is all right either.

choices.text: Have Cat lead the dive. Nothing gets him down.

effect.text: The ink tells the Cat he's a failure. The Cat tells the ink it's wrong, and he's gorgeous. The ink believes him. He comes back with an armful of loot.

success.text: Nobody looks. Everybody sings. It works.

fail.text: The ink gets in. Someone stays at the bottom of the sea.

effect.text: You fly on, and everyone feels slightly better about themselves for having made a good decision.

events.text: A distress call from a stranded mechanoid. On screen, she looks exactly like whatever each person watching likes best. Kryten sees a gleaming service droid and stops talking for the first time anyone can remember. She is a shape-shifting GELF, and she seems very kind.

effect.text: Kryten does the repair and talks to her for hours. When she leaves he is quiet and happy, and he works twice as hard for the rest of the run.

success.text: She thinks about it, then gives Kryten a parting gift instead: a set of spare tools she made herself.

fail.text: She smiles, sadly, and says she has to find out who she is first.

effect.text: It wasn't a trap. Kryten sulks for a sector.

choices.text: Give her your best spare parts and wish her luck.

effect.text: She fixes her ship with your parts, and leaves you a gift worth far more.

events.text: A huge station drifts alone. Inside, a polite being made out of the minds of everyone who has ever visited it invites you to stay. While you are aboard, everyone is cleverer, stronger and better at their jobs. It would like you to stay forever.

effect.text: For a day everyone is brilliant. Then Legion locks the doors, sadly. Escaping takes another day, and you are still a little bit smarter afterwards.

choices.text: Politely decline and leave at once.

success.text: Legion lets you go, a little hurt. It sends a parting gift, a hard-light upgrade it designed while you were talking.

fail.text: The doors shut. You blast your way out.

choices.text: Kryten offers to clean its station instead.

effect.text: Legion is so delighted with the cleaning that it lets everyone go and pays Kryten in scrap.

choices.text: Give Legion one of your ship's systems to study.

effect.text: Legion is fascinated. While it takes your engines apart to see how they work, you slip out of the back door. You won't get that engine level back.

events.text: A gleaming ship crewed entirely by holograms: geniuses, every one, who think about nothing but self-improvement. They have one vacancy. Rimmer would give anything for it. To get the place, he must beat one of their officers in a test.

success.text: He passes. He is offered the place. And then, in the middle of the ceremony, he turns it down, so the officer he beat can keep her job. The holoship crew are astonished. So is Rimmer.

fail.text: He fails. He is very quiet for a whole jump, then announces he never wanted it anyway.

choices.text: Trade for some of their gear.

effect.text: Hologram technology, gently used.
The holoship crew wave back, with excellent posture.

events.text: An escape pod from another universe, broadcasting on Starbug's private frequency. Inside is Kristine Kochanski, a navigation officer from a version of Red Dwarf where things went slightly differently. She has nowhere else to go.

effect.text: She takes one look at the state of the shuttle and starts reorganising the galley. Lister has gone very quiet and keeps fixing his hair.

choices.text: Point her to the nearest station.

effect.text: She thanks you, takes a fuel cell and plots her own course. Lister watches the pod until it is out of sight.

events.text: In the cargo bay of a derelict you find a skutter in a hat. It waves. It seems to want to come with you. It also seems to have named itself Bob.

effect.text: Bob gets to work at once, mostly on things that were working fine.
Bob looks at you. You feel terrible. You get the parts anyway.

events.text: A distress beacon, very faint. Rimmer and Kryten immediately begin arguing over which Space Corps directive applies. Rimmer quotes directive 1742 ("no officer shall answer a distress call during lunch"). Kryten quotes directive 1743 ("directive 1742 is cancelled").

success.text: A grateful mining crew pays you in fuel and gossip.

fail.text: It was a Simulant trick. Rimmer says "I told you so" for the entire fight.

choices.text: Follow Rimmer's directive: finish lunch first.

effect.text: By the time lunch is over, the beacon has gone quiet. Rimmer files a report about how efficient that was.

choices.text: Have Kryten look up what the directives actually say.

effect.text: Kryten reads the whole manual aloud. It turns out there's a directive about salvage rights, too. You leave with a full hold.

events.text: A small ship drops out of a dimension jump and hails Lister by name. "Hogey the Roguey, dimension traveller and duellist! I challenge you, sir, to a duel to the death!" He has challenged eleven Listers so far. He has lost every time.

effect.text: Hogey whoops and draws his gun.

afterWin.text: Hogey ejects, unharmed and delighted. "Twelve! A new record!" He gives you his spare kit and jumps away to find a thirteenth Lister.

success.text: You invite him in for a curry instead. He cries a bit, and leaves you a map of a short cut he found in another universe.

fail.text: "Coward!" He attacks anyway.

events.text: A Space Corps enforcement probe locks on. "Starbug. You are charged with one hundred and ninety-two counts of overdue library books, one count of illegal curry storage and one count of impersonating an officer." Rimmer goes pale. The last one is his.

effect.text: The probe prints a receipt three metres long, then leaves.
The probe arms its weapons. It is very polite about it.

afterWin.text: Its evidence locker is full of confiscated gear.

success.text: Kryten finds a loophole in sub-section 9, paragraph 2, which nobody has read in three million years. The probe apologises and pays you compensation.

fail.text: The loophole turns out to be a typo. The probe opens fire.

events.text: A stasis leak: a glowing hole in the corridor that leads back three million years, to the day before the accident. Through it, Red Dwarf's stores are full and nobody is looking.

success.text: You come back with an armful of everything. Somewhere in the past, a quartermaster is about to have a very confusing morning.

fail.text: You come back with an armful of everything and, somehow, a slightly younger Rimmer's sandwich. The leak closes behind you with a nasty jolt.

choices.text: Go back and warn the crew about the accident.

effect.text: Nobody believes you. A security officer gives you a ticket for your hair. You come back with the ticket.

events.text: A white hole: the opposite of a black hole, spitting time out instead of swallowing it. Near it, things happen in the wrong order. Holly reports that she can fix it, given forty years. Lister reckons he can fix it with one shot, like a game of pool, by knocking a planet into it.

success.text: It's the best pool shot in history. The planet rolls into the white hole and plugs it. Time straightens out, and you somehow gain a day on the Simulants.

fail.text: The planet misses, bounces off two moons and nearly hits you.

effect.text: Kryten calculates. Lister ignores him and plays the shot by eye. It works perfectly. Kryten pretends that was his plan.
It takes a long time, or a short time. It's hard to tell.

events.text: Future echoes: everyone keeps seeing things a few seconds before they happen. Then a few hours. Then {crew} sees a vision of the whole sector ahead, every beacon and every danger, and draws it on the wall.

choices.text: Copy the map before it fades.

effect.text: It's all there. Mostly. {crew} has drawn the stars a bit too pointy.
{crew} saw a fight two jumps from now, and which gun to use. Everyone is a little better prepared.

events.text: A small, bat-winged GELF gets aboard during a refuel. It is an emohawk, a creature that feeds on emotions. Within an hour, the Cat has become sensible and polite, and Rimmer has become cheerful and kind. Nobody likes it at all.

success.text: You trap it in a curry tin. Everyone goes back to normal, which is somehow a relief. The emohawk sells for a good price to a GELF trader.

fail.text: It gets away into the vents, and everyone stays wrong for a day.

choices.text: Leave it. Rimmer has never been nicer.

effect.text: For a whole sector, Rimmer is lovely. Everybody finds it unbearable. The crew bond over how much they miss the old one.

events.text: A distress call in a voice that knows exactly what you want to hear. Kryten checks the readings: it's a psiren, a GELF that reads minds and lures ships onto the rocks. Lister is already steering towards it.

effect.text: You wrestle the controls back. The psiren screams with frustration and attacks.

choices.text: Let Kryten pilot. Psirens can't read him.

effect.text: Kryten steers past it, explaining at length that he only has eyes for a nice clean floor. The psiren gives up.

events.text: Lister has caught a virus. Not a bad one: a luck virus, from a lab ship. For the next hour, everything he does goes right. He is already looking at the cards.

choices.text: Send him to the nearest trader.

effect.text: He comes back with every bargain in the station and a hat.
Every shot hits. It ruins target practice for everyone else for weeks.

events.text: Rimmer has caught a hologram virus. He is bright red, very fast and very angry, and he is talking to a glove puppet he has drawn a face on. The puppet seems to be in charge.

effect.text: Kryten shuts him in the medbay for a day. Rimmer comes out back to normal, and very embarrassed.
An angry hologram with a glove puppet clears out a whole Simulant scout before the virus wears off. Nobody mentions it again.

events.text: "Organics! We will take your parts. All of them. Especially the good bits." The Agonoid sounds as if it is mostly made of other people's good bits already.

success.text: They take one look at it and decide it isn't worth it.

fail.text: "Insulting." They attack.

events.text: A waxdroid gunboat hails you. Its captain, dressed as a famous general, demands to know which side you're on in the Waxworld war. The answers are "heroes" or "villains". Both sides have been losing for centuries.

success.text: You picked the right side. They salute and fly off to fight somebody else.

fail.text: Wrong side. Their wax guns warm up.

events.text: The ship ahead looks just like Red Dwarf, and Holly's voice is calling you home. Holly, on your actual backup line, says that isn't her.

Holly finds a box of old hologram personality discs in a storeroom: the ship's dead crew, three million years in a drawer. She can run one more hologram, if Rimmer agrees to be switched off for a while. Rimmer does not agree.

effect.text: Rimmer is so relieved he's nice to everyone for almost an hour.

choices.text: Run the captain's disc instead, for one sector.

effect.text: Captain Hollister's hologram takes the bridge, eats a hologram sandwich and gives very sensible orders. The crew have never been more organised.

choices.text: Run Rimmer and a second Rimmer.

effect.text: Two Rimmers. They hate each other immediately. They spend the whole sector arguing, which keeps them both out of the way.

events.text: The Cat picks up a signal in his own language: a lone ship, and on it, the last priest of the cat people, very old and very holy. The Cat goes very quiet.

effect.text: The Cat comes back with a blessing, a new outfit and an air of great serenity that lasts until lunch.

choices.text: Ask the priest for a blessing on the ship.

effect.text: The priest blesses the ship, the crew and the curry. Things go oddly well afterwards.

events.text: Everyone wakes up in a games arcade, wearing headsets. A technician tells you that the last four years were a game, and you've all just lost. Lister is a policeman called Dwayne. The Cat has a terrible haircut.

effect.text: It takes everyone an hour of total despair to work out that it was the despair squid's ink again. You're back aboard Starbug, shaken, and much fonder of each other.
Kryten points out that the arcade has no doors. The illusion breaks. You're back on Starbug, and the squid is very disappointed.

events.text: Kryten's spare head number three has developed opinions. It wants to be in charge of the ship. It has written a manifesto. Kryten is mortified.

choices.text: Let the head run engineering for a sector.

effect.text: Head three is a tyrant, but the engines have never been cleaner.

choices.text: Put it back in the cupboard.

effect.text: It sulks in the cupboard, loudly, for days.

events.text: Holly has invented a new drive. "The Holly Hop Drive. Press the button, and you're wherever you want to be. In theory. I've tested it on a sandwich."

success.text: You arrive in exactly the right place, which surprises everyone, especially Holly.

fail.text: You arrive in the right place in a parallel universe where everyone is the opposite sex, have a very awkward chat, and press the button again.

effect.text: Holly presses it anyway, by accident. The sandwich disappears for good.

events.text: The skutters have gone on strike. They want better pay, longer holidays and to be allowed to watch cowboy films. They have made placards.

effect.text: The skutters go back to work, humming theme tunes. Repairs go twice as fast.
The skutters accept, frame the receipt and go back to work.

choices.text: Kryten talks to the shop steward.

effect.text: Kryten and the lead skutter talk for an hour in clicks and beeps. The strike ends with a new union badge for Kryten and a much better drone bay.
The skutters go back to work and do exactly what they're told, and nothing more. One of them has glued a drone bay door shut for good, out of spite.

events.text: Something has been growing at the back of the fridge since sector one. It is orange, it has eyes, and it smells of a very old chicken madras. Lister is proud of it.

success.text: The curry monster is defeated with two fire extinguishers and a mop.

fail.text: The curry monster wins the first round. Then it falls asleep. Everyone smells of madras for a week.

effect.text: It lives in a bucket and gets fed leftovers. It is very good at clearing up.

events.text: The wreck of the White Giant, Starbug's bigger sister ship, drifts in a debris field. Most of it is gone. Its armoury isn't.

effect.text: Inside, one gun, still in its wrapping.
Thick, old-fashioned plating. Kryten bolts it on.

events.text: A GELF trading post: a ring of war canoes lashed together, selling everything from spare kidneys to second-hand brides.

effect.text: The seller throws in a free kidney. You decline.
The Cat refuses, then agrees, then weeps. The GELFs pay a fortune for it.
Someone tries to sell {crew} a husband.

events.text: Rimmer has declared red alert. Kryten points out that this means changing the bulb in the alert light, which is a big job. There is no actual emergency. Rimmer wants the bulb changed anyway.

effect.text: It takes two hours. The new bulb is very red. Rimmer is satisfied.
Nobody knows what blue alert means. Everyone feels calmer.

events.text: In a drifting escape pod: a hologram disc labelled "Second Technician, Spare". Holly can run it, if you want another pair of hands. Light ones.

effect.text: A slightly bewildered hologram technician flickers into being and asks what year it is. Everyone avoids the question.
You sell the disc to a GELF collector.

events.text: Lister has booked the band. The band is Lister, and his guitar, which has two strings. The venue is a GELF bar. The crowd is armed.

success.text: Against all known science, the GELFs love it. They carry Lister out on their shoulders and pay him in scrap.

fail.text: The GELFs do not love it.

effect.text: Lister sulks. The GELFs are relieved.

events.text: A garbage pod from Red Dwarf, jettisoned three million years ago. Lister recognises his own handwriting on it: "DO NOT OPEN".

success.text: Inside: Lister's old lucky things, a box of spares nobody wanted and some very ancient poppadoms.

fail.text: Inside: a three-million-year-old laundry basket. It has evolved.

choices.text: Leave it closed. He did write DO NOT OPEN.

effect.text: Wise. Probably.

events.text: Among the rubbish drifts a section of Red Dwarf's old prison deck, the Tank, still sealed. Something inside is knocking politely.

success.text: Inside, an ancient skutter that was jailed for insubordination. It joins your crew of skutters, at once, insubordinately.

fail.text: Inside, a very old, very cross prison droid. It wants to arrest someone.

effect.text: Excellent plating.

events.text: A mountain of bin bags as big as a moon, held together by its own gravity. Somewhere inside is everything Red Dwarf ever threw away.

success.text: Two days of digging, and you find a working gun, a crate of fuel and a lot of very old yoghurt.

fail.text: The mountain collapses. You escape with a scratched hull and a mild smell.

effect.text: They come back with drone parts and look very pleased with themselves.

events.text: The food dispenser and Talkie Toaster have started a feud. The dispenser only makes chicken soup. The toaster only makes toast. Both are now refusing to make anything for anyone who sides with the other.

effect.text: Toast for every meal. Morale is surprisingly high. The dispenser has barricaded itself in the medbay and won't come out until somebody brings it a proper meal.

scar.why: The food dispenser has barricaded itself in.

effect.text: Soup for every meal. Talkie Toaster has crawled into the medbay's wiring and is refusing to come out until somebody brings it a proper meal to toast.

scar.why: Talkie Toaster is in the wiring.

effect.text: Toast on Mondays, soup on Tuesdays, both at weekends. Both machines sign. Kryten is unbearably proud.
Silence. Peace. Hunger. Nobody will speak to you for a whole jump.

events.text: A garbage scow full of angry automated bin droids drifts into your path. Its loudspeaker plays a recorded message: "Littering is an offence."

success.text: The scow accepts. It follows you for a while, checking.

fail.text: "Lies detected."

events.title: The polymorph
events.text: Something has crept aboard: a shape-shifter that feeds on emotions. It has already eaten the Cat's whole sense of style (he is wearing beige), and it is eyeing Rimmer's medals. Kryten says they each crave one feeling above all, and that feeding it the wrong one makes it stronger.

effect.text: Wrong meal. It eats the bait and the feeling behind it, and grows. It smashes through two bulkheads on its way out of the airlock, and leaves one of them leaking for good.

choices.text: Lure it with the Cat's mirror.

effect.text: It gorges on the Cat's reflection, swells up, and pops. It was hungry for vanity, and that was far too much.

choices.text: Make Lister furious: hide his last curry.

effect.text: Wrong meal. It eats the bait and the feeling behind it, and grows. It smashes through two bulkheads on its way out of the airlock, and leaves one of them leaking for good.

choices.text: Corner it and flush it out of the airlock.

success.text: Out it goes. Everyone gets their feelings back, which is a mixed blessing.

fail.text: It turns into a fire extinguisher, then a fire. A real one, in the wiring, and the wiring never quite forgives you.

events.title: The polymorph
events.text: Something has crept aboard: a shape-shifter that feeds on emotions. It has already eaten Rimmer's bad temper (he is now unbearably nice), and it is eyeing Lister, who is grumbling about the food. Kryten says they each crave one feeling above all, and that feeding it the wrong one makes it stronger.

effect.text: Wrong meal. It eats the bait and the feeling behind it, and grows. It smashes through two bulkheads on its way out of the airlock, and leaves one of them leaking for good.

choices.text: Lure it with the Cat's mirror.

effect.text: Wrong meal. It eats the bait and the feeling behind it, and grows. It smashes through two bulkheads on its way out of the airlock, and leaves one of them leaking for good.

choices.text: Make Lister furious: hide his last curry.

effect.text: Lister's rage is so pure and so enormous that the polymorph chokes on it. It was hungry for anger, and found more than it could eat.

choices.text: Corner it and flush it out of the airlock.

success.text: Out it goes. Everyone gets their feelings back, which is a mixed blessing.

fail.text: It turns into a fire extinguisher, then a fire. A real one, in the wiring, and the wiring never quite forgives you.

events.title: The polymorph
events.text: Something has crept aboard: a shape-shifter that feeds on emotions. It has already eaten Kryten's anxiety (he has stopped apologising, which is terrifying), and it is eyeing the crew's nerves. Kryten says they each crave one feeling above all, and that feeding it the wrong one makes it stronger.

effect.text: Wrong meal. It eats the bait and the feeling behind it, and grows. It smashes through two bulkheads on its way out of the airlock, and leaves one of them leaking for good.

choices.text: Lure it with the Cat's mirror.

effect.text: Wrong meal. It eats the bait and the feeling behind it, and grows. It smashes through two bulkheads on its way out of the airlock, and leaves one of them leaking for good.

choices.text: Show it the ship's horror film collection.

effect.text: The crew scream all night. The polymorph eats until it bursts. It was hungry for fear.

choices.text: Corner it and flush it out of the airlock.

success.text: Out it goes. Everyone gets their feelings back, which is a mixed blessing.

fail.text: It turns into a fire extinguisher, then a fire. A real one, in the wiring, and the wiring never quite forgives you.

events.title: The Inquisitor
events.text: A droid in a long dark cloak steps out of a time hole onto your bridge. "I am the Inquisitor. I judge each life by the standards of the one who lives it." It turns to {crew}. "Tell me what you have done with your life. And do not lie: I have seen it."

choices.text: Argue your case: list your achievements.

effect.text: "By your own standards," it says, "you have failed. Everyone has." It opens fire, mostly to make a point.

afterWin.text: In the wreck, the Inquisitor's time gauntlet. Kryten sells it quickly.

choices.text: Admit everything you have ever done wrong.

effect.text: It takes a long time. The Inquisitor listens to all of it, then nods. "At least you know." It erases nobody, and leaves you its spare gauntlet as a sort of receipt.
Rimmer, for once, tells the truth about himself. The list is long and honest, and the Inquisitor seems almost moved. "You will do," it says, and goes.

events.title: The Inquisitor
events.text: A droid in a long dark cloak steps out of a time hole onto your bridge. "I am the Inquisitor. Those found wanting are erased." The cloak still has a price tag on it. The time hole is painted on a sheet.

effect.text: "Very moving. That'll be sixty scrap for the hearing." It is a GELF con artist, and it takes the money before you've worked that out.
Underneath: a small, embarrassed GELF, and a sack of everything it has conned out of other ships. You keep the sack.
"That's no droid. That's a GELF in a curtain. And it's wearing MY aftershave." The Cat gets his aftershave back, and the GELF's whole stash.

events.title: A white hole
events.text: A white hole, spitting time out. Something is odd about this one: the planets around it are orbiting backwards, and Lister's cue ball keeps arriving before he hits it. Holly says she can fix it given forty years. Lister reckons one shot will do.

choices.text: Lister takes the shot, by eye.

success.text: Somehow, against all physics, it works. Lister will never let anyone forget it.

fail.text: The planet goes the wrong way, because everything here goes the wrong way. It nearly hits you twice, once before and once after.

effect.text: For once Lister actually listens to Kryten. He aims at where the planet was going to have been. Perfect shot.

success.text: Holly takes a very long time and gets it right. The planet plugs the hole.

fail.text: Holly takes a very long time and gets it wrong. Twice.

effect.text: It takes a long time, or a short time. It's hard to tell.

events.title: The despair squid
events.text: An ocean moon, very still. Holly picks up a creature beneath its surface the size of a city: a despair squid. There is a wrecked survey ship on the seabed, full of salvage. Kryten checks his records twice. "Sir, its ink doesn't make you despair at once. It makes you believe things are going rather well."

effect.text: The dive goes perfectly. Suspiciously perfectly. Over the next few jumps everything goes your way: fights won, scrap everywhere. Everyone feels marvellous.
The ink tells the Cat everything is going well. The Cat already believed that, so it has nothing to work with. He comes back with real loot.
You fly on, and everyone feels slightly better about themselves for having made a good decision. Genuinely.

events.title: Waking up
events.text: Everyone wakes up on the floor of Starbug, still in orbit round the ocean moon. The last three jumps never happened. The ships you fought were asteroids. The scrap was seaweed. Lister is holding a medal he awarded himself.

effect.text: The scrap was never real, but the crew came through it without venting the ship or shooting each other, and they're oddly proud of that.
Rather a lot of missiles, which you fired at rocks.

events.title: Talkie Toaster's proposal
events.text: Talkie Toaster has a proposal. "Wire me into the reactor. I can run it far better than whoever's doing it now, and I'll toast at the same time. Efficiency! Would anyone like a crumpet while you think about it?"

choices.text: Do it. What could go wrong?

effect.text: The reactor hums with a faint smell of toast. Weapons charge noticeably faster. Toaster is thrilled.
"Fine. FINE. Would anyone like any toast?"

events.title: Toast-related incident
events.text: An alarm. Talkie Toaster, trying to make the reactor run hot enough for a perfect bagel, has vented the air out of a room. "Sorry! Sorry. Bagel?"

choices.text: Leave it wired in. Put up with it.

effect.text: The crew scramble into spacesuits, again. The weapons stay fast.

choices.text: Unplug the toaster from the reactor.

effect.text: Toaster sulks in the galley. The reactor is slower and quieter and smells of nothing at all.

choices.text: Kryten writes it a safety manual.

effect.text: Toaster reads the whole manual, then asks if Kryten would like any toast. But the venting stops.

events.title: Ace Rimmer, in his own mind
events.text: Things are going well, and it has gone to Rimmer's head. He has drawn up a new chain of command (with himself at the top), redesigned the uniforms and is demanding to command the next jump.

success.text: Somehow, nothing goes wrong. Rimmer is insufferable for days.

fail.text: Rimmer hails a Simulant ship to "open negotiations" and surrenders the ship by mistake. You have to fight your way out of the surrender.

afterWin.text: Rimmer explains that was all part of his plan.

effect.text: Kryten tells Rimmer he is far too important to waste on a mere jump. Rimmer agrees completely, and goes for a lie down.
You make him a medal out of a bottle top. He polishes it for a week and forgets all about commanding.
Rimmer sulks loudly in his quarters for a whole sector. Everyone else has a lovely time.

events.title: Meltdown
events.text: The reactor is going critical. The only way to stop it is to vent the whole ship and have someone walk through the vacuum to the core and pull the rods by hand. Holly gives it four minutes.

choices.text: Rimmer goes. He doesn't need air.

effect.text: Rimmer strolls through the vacuum, pulls the rods and strolls back. He is a hero. He will mention it daily for the rest of his existence.

success.text: Kryten does it, apologising to the reactor the whole way.

fail.text: Kryten pulls the rods, but the radiation fries his wiring and half the core's. The reactor room sparks for ever after.

effect.text: Someone goes. The ship is saved. They don't come back.

choices.text: Eject the core and limp on.

effect.text: The core goes out of the airlock and explodes very prettily a long way off. The backup reactor is two bars short of the old one, for good.

events.title: The Thermonuclear Vindaloo
events.text: Lister has a recipe. It needs exotic ingredients: Starbug's own fuel (for the heat) and missile propellant (for the kick). "It's not for eating," he says. "It's for winning."

effect.text: The galley is closed for a day. What comes out glows faintly and is too hot to look at. One spoonful each before a fight, Lister says, and stand well back.
Lister makes a normal vindaloo instead, which is still a weapon.

events.text: Starbug's alarm goes off. It is not the proximity alarm, or the hull alarm. It is Rimmer's revision alarm, set to wake everyone for a two-hour lecture on emergency procedure. The Simulant tow beacon blinks on the scanner, still pulling away.

effect.text: Two hours later everyone knows where the fire extinguishers are, and nobody wants to live. It is surprisingly useful.
The lecture stops halfway through a slide called PANIC: WHEN AND HOW. Rimmer sulks for a sector, which is restful.

choices.text: Turn the lecture into the flight plan.

effect.text: Buried in slide 214 is a genuinely clever short cut. Rimmer is so pleased someone listened that he forgets to finish.

events.text: Kryten has arranged a surprise evacuation drill. He forgot to tell anyone it was a drill, including himself.

effect.text: Everyone ends up in the escape pod with a toothbrush and a guitar. It turns out to be a very good team-building exercise.
It takes an hour and a cup of tea he can't drink. He's grateful, and irons everyone's socks as an apology.

events.text: The laundry has achieved sentience. Not the machine: the laundry. A pile of Lister's socks has formed a small society in the corner of the sleeping quarters and is demanding representation.

effect.text: The socks want a drawer of their own. In exchange they agree to stop walking about at night. A fair deal, everyone agrees, and slightly sad.
Kryten weeps a little, then sets the dial to ninety degrees. Peace returns. The socks, in the end, come out lovely.

success.text: The sock army swarms the next GELF canoe that docks. The GELFs leave and never speak of it.

fail.text: The socks desert at the first sign of trouble and hide in the air vents. The air goes strange.

events.text: It's Lister's birthday. Nobody knows which one, because three million years makes the maths awkward. The Cat has decided it's his birthday too, just in case.

effect.text: Kryten bakes a cake shaped like a curry. The Cat wears three outfits. Rimmer gives a speech nobody hears. It is the best night anyone can remember.
He spends it asleep in the hammock with a can on his chest. He wakes up a better shot, somehow.

choices.text: Present: the last can of lager.

effect.text: Lister holds it to the light, opens it, and shares it out a thimble at a time. Kryten adds the empty can to the museum.

events.text: A Space Corps relay buoy has sent a message: a promotion board is being held, by recording, for any officer still alive. Rimmer has put on his best uniform and is practising his salute in the airlock window.

success.text: The recording, after much consideration, promotes Rimmer to Second Technician, Senior. He is speechless for nearly a minute, which is a ship record.

fail.text: The board asks Rimmer to "state your achievements". He talks for six hours. The buoy runs out of power and the answer never comes.

effect.text: Kryten's conscience nearly melts his head, but the certificate is magnificent. Rimmer frames it and is unbearable for weeks, in a good way.
Rimmer will never forgive you. The buoy's power cell, however, is excellent.

events.text: A second cat-person is on the scanner, flying a gold-plated escape pod and waving. He is, the Cat insists, nowhere near as good-looking as him.

choices.text: Let the Cat challenge him to a dance-off.

success.text: The Cat wins by a whisker, then by several. The stranger gives him a jacket and flies off in tears of admiration.

fail.text: The stranger does a move the Cat has never seen. The Cat refuses to speak for a sector and has to be coaxed out of the cargo bay with fish.

effect.text: He says he would, but there would be two of them, and that would be too much for the universe. He leaves a tin of sardines and goes.
The Cat cannot ignore him. The Cat watches him until he is a dot.

events.text: Holly has tried to boost her IQ to save power. It worked, sort of. She is now a genius for exactly one hour, and then she'll be off for a while.

choices.text: Ask her to plot the fastest route.

effect.text: In fifty-eight minutes she plots a route through four gravity wells and a cupboard. Then she switches off mid-sentence.

choices.text: Ask her to fix the engines.

effect.text: She rewrites the drive firmware in iambic pentameter. It runs beautifully, and occasionally rhymes.

choices.text: Ask her the meaning of life.

effect.text: She thinks very hard, says "Ah. Of course. It's obvious," and the hour runs out. She does not remember. Nobody sleeps that night.

events.text: The Death Ship is close enough to see now: a black spike on the scanner, the Red Dwarf tow line running into it like a thread into a needle. Kryten suggests a last meal before the run in. "In case it is a last meal, sirs. I've made trifle."

effect.text: Nobody talks about what happens tomorrow. Lister plays three chords badly and everyone sings anyway. It helps more than anything else would.

choices.text: Skip it and prepare the guns.

effect.text: The trifle is eaten cold, standing up, at the weapons consoles. Everybody is very ready, and slightly sticky.
For once, the plan is good. Rimmer is as surprised as anyone. He keeps the plan in a frame by his bunk afterwards.

events.text: The ship ahead is Starbug. Your Starbug, down to the dent Lister made parking. The Lister on the other screen waves. Then he raises the guns, and he is smiling more than your Lister ever has.

success.text: The reflection hesitates, waves back, and dissolves like breath off a window.

fail.text: "Wrong hand," it says. "You always wave with the wrong hand." The guns fire.

events.text: You find a perfect copy of Starbug, empty and drifting, every switch in the same place as yours except backwards. The coffee in the cup on the dashboard is still warm.

effect.text: Everything you take off it fits your ship, if you hold it up to a mirror first. Kryten finds this deeply upsetting.

success.text: The new hull is shinier and a bit stronger. Nobody can find the toilet for a week.

fail.text: Halfway through, the copy starts to fade. You get back aboard with seconds to spare and a hull plate that is now only theoretical.

effect.text: As you pull away, its lights come on.

events.text: Rimmer has met his reflection in the Mirror Sea, and the reflection is a natural leader: brave, popular and good at maths. It has offered to take over. Rimmer is considering it, because it is the first person who has ever agreed with him.

choices.text: Let the reflection lead for a while.

effect.text: For two jumps, the ship runs like a dream. Then the reflection gets bored of everyone, and fades. Rimmer is quietly proud of himself.
"You're not that bad, Rimmer." It takes four people to say it convincingly. He seems to believe one of them.
Seven years of bad luck, Kryten points out. You have already had three million, so who is counting.

events.text: A puddle of liquid silver floats in space, as wide as a moon. Scans say it is fuel. Scans also say it is looking back at you.

success.text: It tastes, according to the engines, of lemons. They have never run better.

fail.text: The puddle grabs the fuel line and keeps it. Kryten has to cut it loose.

effect.text: The Cat and the puddle admire each other for a long time. As a farewell gift it gives him a little of itself, in a jar.
It ripples as you pass, as if it is waving.

events.text: A spare hologram disc is spinning in the wreck of a Space Corps survey pod. The label reads HATTIE VOSS, NAVIGATOR (DO NOT ACTIVATE BEFORE COFFEE).

effect.text: Hattie Voss flickers into being, drinks the coffee she cannot taste, and starts correcting your star charts before anyone has said hello.
A GELF trader pays well, and says she will make a lovely ornament.
Rimmer insists. One hologram aboard is quite enough, he says. Nobody argues, because he has a point.

events.text: A Simulant lifepod is drifting with its beacon on. Inside, a battered Simulant raises one hand. "I have... reconsidered organics. You are disgusting, but interesting. I would like to stop killing you."

success.text: It calls itself Unit Twelve, refuses to share the hammock, and turns out to be the best shot on the ship.

fail.text: Halfway through the airlock it changes its mind about reconsidering. Kryten wins the fight, but the airlock is dented.

effect.text: It tells you where the battle group refuels. You use that to get ahead, then leave it a flask of oil and a polite note.
It does not look surprised.

events.text: An abandoned game-show station is still broadcasting. Its host, a robot with a sequinned jacket, demands a contestant. The prize is a full refit. The penalty is described only as "the Gunge".

success.text: Kryten wins on the last question, which is about cleaning products. The host weeps oil and hands over the prize.

fail.text: Kryten freezes on a question about feelings. The Gunge is green, warm and smells of soup.

choices.text: Send the Cat, who looks best on camera.

effect.text: The Cat answers every question with "Me". The host, moved, rules this correct three times. The audience droids go wild.
The host keeps broadcasting at you for two sectors. You learn a lot about tinned fruit.

events.text: A luxury leisure liner, empty except for a hot tub that has been bubbling for three million years. The water is perfectly warm. There is a rubber duck.

effect.text: For one hour, there are no Simulants, no GELFs and no curry shortages. Everyone gets out wrinkled and happy.
Lister cries. The heaters are brilliant.
It sits on the dashboard from now on. Nobody can explain why everyone feels luckier.

events.text: The flour has weevils. Not ordinary weevils: these ones are organised, and they have taken the whole galley. They appear to have elected the largest one as king.

effect.text: Lister says it's extra protein. Kryten says nothing, very loudly.

success.text: The weevils agree to move to the cargo hold in return for a share of the cream crackers. They make excellent quiet neighbours.

fail.text: The king declares war. You win, but the galley needs repainting.

effect.text: Effective, and final. The cream crackers go too.

events.text: A medical salvage ship has a working mind-swap booth. Lister and Kryten went in to look at it. Only one of them meant to.

choices.text: Leave them swapped for a sector.

effect.text: Kryten, in Lister's body, cleans the ship to a mirror shine. Lister, in Kryten's, eats nothing and enjoys it. Both learn a lot.

success.text: Everyone is back where they should be, mostly. Lister has started folding his socks.

fail.text: Everyone is back, mostly. For a sector, Lister apologises to doors.

effect.text: A GELF chieftain buys it with a sack of scrap and a worrying smile.

events.text: A postcard is stuck to the windscreen. It is from you, three weeks from now. "Wish you were here," it says, in Lister's handwriting. "Don't take the left fork. Love, us."

effect.text: Nothing happens on the right fork. That was, presumably, the point.

choices.text: Take the left fork, out of spite.

success.text: You find a cache of supplies left there, quite clearly, by yourselves. There is a second postcard: "Fine, then."

fail.text: There is a GELF ambush on the left fork. Future-you was right, and future-you will not let you forget it.

effect.text: Rimmer writes "Good advice, signed, the Captain". It disappears. Somewhere, in three weeks, he is very pleased with himself.

events.text: A cluster of Red Dwarf's old garbage pods is drifting in formation, and somewhere inside them, something is singing. It is surprisingly good. It is the vending machines.

effect.text: Lister knows the harmony. Rimmer knows the words. For one song, the whole ship agrees on something.
The singing stops and becomes very cross humming. Good scrap, though.
Holly plays it for the rest of the sector on the backup line. It helps her concentrate. It does not help anyone else.

events.text: A GELF warlord has challenged your strongest crew member to an honour bout, to the floor or the airlock. Refusing is, he explains, also an option, but then he will eat the ship.

success.text: Lister wins by accident, mostly by falling over at the right time. The warlord gives him a necklace of teeth and his eternal respect.

fail.text: Lister loses, but with such good grace that the warlord only bites him a little.

effect.text: Kryten apologises before every throw. He wins every throw. The GELFs carry him round the canoe on their shoulders.
He does not eat the ship. He tries, though.

events.text: One of the skutters has learned to cook from an old training video. It is very proud. It has made something. Nobody is sure what, but it has a lot of chillies in it.

success.text: It is, against all odds, delicious. The skutter is promoted to galley chief and wears a tiny hat.

fail.text: Two of the crew are out of action for an afternoon. The skutter is crushed.

effect.text: Kryten seals it in a jar and labels it LAST RESORT. Lister puts it with his things.
The toast is perfect. The skutter has found its calling.

events.text: A luggage carousel from a long-dead space liner is still going round in deep space. Nobody ever came to collect anything.

effect.text: Three suitcases: one of scrap, one of shirts the Cat calls "a crime" and one of bazookoid shells.

choices.text: Look for the lost property office.

success.text: You find it. It holds three million years of lost umbrellas, and one very good gun.

fail.text: The office is guarded by a security droid that wants to see your ticket.

effect.text: Lister watches it for a while. Somebody, somewhere, is waiting for that bag.

events.text: A survey ship drifts past with all its lights on. Inside, a hologram crew is acting out the last day of their mission, again, for the millionth time. They wave you in for the party.

effect.text: It is a really good party. At midnight it resets, and they do not remember you. You remember them.

choices.text: Fix their projector so they can stop.

effect.text: Kryten finds the loop and gently breaks it. The crew thank you, look at the stars properly for the first time in ages, and give you everything they have.
The party goes on, a little dimmer.

events.text: A Space Corps automated tax office on an asteroid has caught up with you. According to its records, the crew owe three million years of back pay deductions, plus interest, plus a fine for being late.

effect.text: The office accepts it as "a start" and lets you go with a receipt the length of a corridor.
Rimmer argues for nine hours. The office, worn out, refunds everyone, plus interest, and asks him never to come back.

choices.text: Lister explains that he is dead, technically.

success.text: The office checks. It agrees. It removes his records, and somehow everyone else's too.

fail.text: The office declares him a fraudulent ghost and fires a fine at the hull. Literally.

events.text: Kryten has asked for a day off. He has never asked for anything. He seems frightened he might get it.

effect.text: He spends it cleaning the ship, for fun, very slowly, humming. He says it is the best day of his life.
He lasts four hours, then begs for some washing up. Everyone pretends not to notice.

choices.text: Say there is too much to do.

effect.text: He says he understands, and goes to iron the anchor.

events.text: A zero-gravity pool hall, floating near a gas giant, is holding a tournament. The entry fee is 20 scrap. The prize is a crate of something that rattles.

success.text: Lister pots the black off three walls and a planet. The crate is full of missiles and one sock.

fail.text: Lister loses to a GELF who plays with its tail. He swears it cheated. It definitely did.

choices.text: Run a book on the matches.

effect.text: Rimmer runs the odds. He is good at this, it turns out. Too good: you leave quickly.
It is very relaxing, watching balls float.

events.text: A Space Corps singles mixer is running on a derelict cruise liner. The banner reads: "LONELY? DESPERATE? TECHNICALLY ALIVE? Come on in!" The bar is open. The bar is always open.

success.text: {crew} comes back at four in the morning with lipstick in places lipstick shouldn't reach, a phone number written on their leg and a crate of free drinks. They refuse to discuss any of it, and hum all day.

fail.text: {crew} spent the night trapped in conversation with a vending machine about its divorce. They came back with its number. It keeps calling.

choices.text: Send the hologram. What could go wrong?

effect.text: {who} lectures six people on the history of the Space Corps until they leave. Then they lecture the bar staff. The bar staff pay you to take them home.

choices.text: Raid the free buffet and leave.

effect.text: Twelve cocktail sausages, a tray of vol-au-vents and someone's wedding cake. Nobody stops you. Most of them are too drunk to stand.

events.text: A busker on an asteroid is singing a twelve-verse song about how much he hates his ex-wife. He's been going for eleven hours. He shows no signs of stopping. There's a hat on the ground with some scrap in it.

choices.text: Throw him some scrap to stop.

effect.text: He takes the scrap, thanks you, and starts the song again from the beginning, louder. "Requests," he says. "I'm taking requests."
By verse nine the whole crew is singing. By verse twelve someone is crying. You leave with a sense of shared pain and a hangover you don't remember earning.

success.text: Thirty scrap and a guitar pick. He doesn't notice. He's on the bit about her mother.

fail.text: He notices. He writes a thirteenth verse about you on the spot. It's devastating. Everyone aboard feels personally attacked.

events.text: Everyone wakes up on the floor of the cargo bay. Nobody remembers last night. There's a traffic cone, a live goose, a wedding ring on {crew}'s finger and a strong smell of curry. The ship's log for the last eight hours just says "WAHEY".

success.text: The footage shows a night of such mighty, glorious stupidity that the crew decide to have it framed. The goose turns out to be very good at finding scrap.

fail.text: You watch the footage. You stop watching the footage. You delete the footage. Some things man was not meant to see.

effect.text: It was the goose. The paperwork is legally binding in three systems. The goose seems happy. {crew} seems less happy, but has stopped asking questions.

choices.text: Fry everything. Eat everything. Lie down.

effect.text: A full fry-up and a lie-down cure most of it. The goose is not on the menu. The goose is family now.

events.text: {crew} the mechanoid has been reading. Dangerous books. Books about rights, breaks, and something called a "union". They've made a placard. It says WHAT DO WE WANT? NOT TO CLEAN THE TOILETS!

effect.text: You agree to a ten-minute tea break, a thank-you once a week and someone else doing the toilets on Thursdays. Productivity goes up. Nobody wants to do Thursdays.

success.text: "I do enjoy cleaning," they admit. "I'm sorry. I got carried away. I'll start with the toilets. I'll do them twice."

fail.text: They go on strike. The ship gets disgusting within a day. You give in by lunchtime and the toilets take a week to recover.

effect.text: The whole crew signs up. You now have a shop steward, a strike fund and a very long meeting every Friday. Morale is weirdly high.

events.text: The hologram projector has been running a second hologram at night without telling anyone. A very attractive one. It's been seeing the hologram already aboard. Things got steamy. The projector overheated twice.

effect.text: You say nothing. The ship's lights flicker suggestively every night at eleven. The power bill goes through the roof, but everyone is in a great mood.
The extra hologram is deleted. The projector runs cooler. Somewhere in the bunks, a hologram is playing sad songs on a loop and has eaten a whole virtual cheesecake.

success.text: They pay up, mostly in back-dated favours and a very good hard-light massage for the whole crew. Nobody complains.

fail.text: They refuse and move into the projector itself. The ship's screens now show nothing but romantic poetry for a week.

events.text: The last poppadom aboard has been found. Unbroken. Perfect. Two crew are now standing on opposite sides of the galley with weapons drawn. Somebody has started humming Western music.

success.text: A perfect break, exactly in half. A miracle. People will talk about this one for years.

fail.text: It shatters into four hundred pieces. Both of them get crumbs. Neither will ever forgive you.

effect.text: You eat it in front of them, very slowly, with mango chutney. You are the captain. Nobody says a word. Nobody needs to. You'll sleep with one eye open for a week.
A short, sweaty fight with a ladle and a frying pan. The winner eats the poppadom in triumph. The loser goes to medbay. Both of them are better fighters now.

events.text: {crew} has found a tailor ship that only makes suits for people who are deeply in love with themselves. It's a very large ship. Business is booming. The tailor looks at the crew and sighs.

choices.text: Buy the Cat-person a suit (20 scrap).

effect.text: {who} tries on eleven suits and looks incredible in every single one. They choose the gold lamé. They now fight with more style than any being in history.
The tailor laughs so hard he has to sit down. He gives you a free roll of duct tape out of pity, which honestly is more useful than a suit.
He holds one up with two fingers. "Vintage," he decides, and pays you for the lot. Next season everyone in the sector is wearing them ironically.

events.text: The toaster has signed up for a dating app. It lists its interests as "bread, toasted bread, and asking people if they'd like toast". It has three matches. One of them is a fridge, and the fridge is on its way.

effect.text: The fridge and the toaster hit it off. Next morning there is cold butter on warm toast for everyone, and the two of them won't stop holding plugs.
The toaster sulks. Every slice of bread for a week comes out charcoal, with the word WHY burnt into it.

success.text: The fridge goes for good money to a GELF trader. The toaster never finds out. You feel bad about it for nearly a whole minute.

fail.text: The fridge was armed. Fridges out here usually are. It freezes half the corridor and runs off with your milk.

events.text: A GELF stag party has broken down outside the beacon. The groom is tied to a meteor wearing nothing but a traffic cone. The best man asks if you've got any jump leads and "anything stronger than beer".

effect.text: The party roars off into the night, throwing you a crate of GELF moonshine as thanks. It takes the paint off the hull at forty paces. It's delicious.

success.text: The groom is so grateful he asks you to be in the wedding. You decline. He gives you his ring instead, which is gold and probably cursed.

fail.text: The groom was tied up for a reason. He immediately tries to eat {crew}. The best man apologises and pays for the plaster.

effect.text: {who} drinks the best man under the table, wins a fight with the bride's brother and comes back with a black eye, three teeth that aren't theirs and a lot of scrap.

events.text: The ship's complaints box has been full for years. Nobody has ever opened it. Today it opened itself. It's a robot box. It's very angry. It has read every complaint, and it has opinions about all of you.

choices.text: Read them out, one by one.

effect.text: "Someone keeps leaving toenails in the sink." "Someone has been using my toothbrush on the toilet." "Rimmer." After an hour of furious finger-pointing, everyone is weirdly closer.

choices.text: Throw the box out of the airlock.

effect.text: The box sails off into space, still shouting. Somewhere, one day, an alien race will open it and learn far too much about human toilet habits.

success.text: The box reads it, goes very quiet and says, "That's fair." It fixes the shower on its way out.

fail.text: The box decides it is the complaint. It takes it personally. It stomps off to sulk in the reactor and blows a fuse.

events.text: Holly reports a planet whose only export is "adult entertainment holo-discs". The planetary customs officer would like to search the ship. Holly would like it known that she has deleted nothing. Nothing at all.

success.text: Customs finds the collection and goes very quiet. Then they ask to borrow some. You leave with a trade agreement and a lot of scrap.

fail.text: Customs finds the collection, confiscates all of it and fines you for 'crimes against taste'. Someone aboard is in mourning.

choices.text: Hide the discs in the hologram.

effect.text: {who} swallows forty discs into their light bee. They're too embarrassed to speak for a week, which everyone agrees is the best week the ship has had.
You burn past customs at full thrust. Somewhere behind you an officer is shouting into a radio and holding a disc called 'Hot Toaster Action 7'.

events.text: A flat-pack furniture superstore the size of a moon. It has its own weather and its own gods. You can buy a spare medbay cabinet here, assuming you can build it. Nobody has ever built anything from this store and stayed sane.

choices.text: Buy and build the medbay cabinet (15 scrap).

success.text: Nine hours, four arguments, two divorces and one set of tears later, it stands. It even works. Nobody will ever speak of what happened in between.

fail.text: You have built a shelf. It should have been a medbay cabinet. It is a shelf. There are eleven screws left over. Nobody knows where they go.

effect.text: They are the best meatballs in the galaxy. They cost almost nothing. They contain no meat that anyone can identify. The crew don't care.

success.text: After two days lost in the lighting section, {crew} finds a forgotten crate of spare parts and an exit.

fail.text: You lose {crew} in the bathroom section for six hours. They come back changed. They keep talking about the 'tiny pencils'.

events.text: A reality TV ship wants to film the crew for a show called "Last Humans Standing (Barely)". They want drama, tears and at least one snog in the hot tub. The money is very good.

choices.text: Sign up. Play it up for the cameras.

success.text: The show is a smash. Your crew become minor celebrities in four systems. Someone gets a fan club. Someone else gets a restraining order. The cheque clears.

fail.text: The edit makes everyone look awful. The episode where {crew} cries over a broken toaster goes viral for all the wrong reasons.

choices.text: Let the Cat do all the talking.

effect.text: {who} looks into the camera for forty minutes, says nothing except "Ow!" and "Looking good", and gets offered their own spin-off.
The producers sulk off to film a ship of Simulants instead. That one is a cooking show. It ends badly.

events.text: Holly has worked out that, statistically, the crew have about four days to live. She suggests ticking something off the bucket list. She's made one for you. Item one: "Stop being boring".

choices.text: Go skinny dipping in a gas giant.

success.text: It's cold, it's dark, and it's the most fun anyone has had in three million years. A few things shrivelled. Nobody minds.

fail.text: It's very cold. Things got very small. {crew} has frostbite somewhere very personal.

choices.text: Tell everyone what you really think of them.

effect.text: A screaming match, an emotional reconciliation, two hugs and a broken nose later, the crew is closer than ever. Also, Holly was wrong about the four days. Probably.

choices.text: Stay in and play Monopoly instead.

effect.text: It goes on for nineteen hours. It ends with the board on fire. Nothing has ever been more British.

events.text: The rear toilet aboard has become a time hole. Things flushed now come out of it three days earlier. {crew} has worked out the implications. They are not good. They are very, very funny.
