effect.text: You flush some scrap. Then you remember that three days ago you found some scrap in the toilet. Which means... You stop thinking about it. You have more scrap now. Probably.
{who} spends a whole day with their arm down the U-bend of time. The toilet works normally again. {who} has to be steam cleaned. Twice.

success.text: You flush a note into the past. Three days ago you found it and avoided an asteroid. Which is why you're alive now. Nice.

fail.text: You flush the note. Three days ago you read it, panicked and crashed into an asteroid. That's why the hull's like this.

events.text: In the middle of a field of floating rubbish, a perfectly good sofa. Leather. Three seats. Only a small stain on one cushion, and you really, really don't want to know what it is.

choices.text: Take it aboard. It's a sofa.

effect.text: It's the best sofa anyone has ever sat on. The stain is never discussed. The crew rest better than they have in years.

success.text: Loose scrap, a missile, a wedding ring and someone's false teeth. A treasure trove. You keep everything except the teeth. You keep the teeth too, actually.

fail.text: There's something living under the cushions. It bites {crew} and runs off into the vents. It might still be in there.

effect.text: You leave a perfectly good sofa floating in space. The crew don't talk to you for a day. You will think about that sofa for the rest of your life.

events.text: On the other side of the mirror you meet your mirror selves. They're exactly like you, but nicer, cleverer, better looking and slightly smug about it. They've invited you round for a dinner party.

effect.text: Their food is better. Their ship is cleaner. Their jokes are funnier. Your mirror self gently asks if you're 'okay', and that's when the fight breaks out.

success.text: Your mirror selves run your ship for a day. They fix everything, clean everything and leave a thank-you note. You hate them. You also have more scrap.

fail.text: They take one look at your ship and swap back early, leaving a note that just says 'how?'.

effect.text: It's very good wine. Your mirror selves are too polite to mention it, which makes it even more fun.

events.text: A waxdroid bar is holding a strip night. The waxdroids are melting under the lights. It's horrifying. It's also, against all odds, drawing a big crowd. The doorman says you look like a fun group.

effect.text: A wax Elvis and a wax Queen Victoria dance in a puddle of their own faces. It's the most disturbing thing you have ever seen. You cannot look away. The crew bond over the shared trauma.
The manager weeps with gratitude and pays you twice what the fan is worth. The dancers can keep their faces on. Mostly.
You back away. The doorman calls you 'prudes'. {crew} goes back in later on their own, and comes back sticky.

events.text: The Inter-Ship Quiz League has a vacancy. The prize is an engine upgrade. The rules are simple: four rounds, no cheating, no weapons. Last year's winners were Simulants. They cheated. With weapons.

effect.text: You're in. The first round is next week. Holly starts revising. So does the toaster, which is worrying.
The organiser groans out loud. You're in. The first round is next week.
You don't enter. Somewhere, the Simulants win again. And cheat again. And shoot the quizmaster again.

events.text: Round one of the quiz league, against a team of very smug GELFs called "Hide and Shriek". Question one: "What is the capital of Jupiter?" Holly buzzes in at once. Holly has no idea.

success.text: "Jupiter Mining Corporation," she says. The quizmaster checks. He blinks. He checks again. Somehow it's right. You win the round on a technicality.

fail.text: "Cheese," says Holly confidently. You lose the round, but scrape into the final on a wildcard because the GELFs ate the other team.

effect.text: {who} answers every question correctly, then apologises for each one. The GELFs are so furious they flip the table. You're in the final.

success.text: A crib sheet in a sleeve, a hologram whispering answers. You win easily. The quizmaster knows. He's impressed.

fail.text: You're caught, disqualified and fined. The GELFs laugh at you all the way to the final.

events.text: The final. You're up against the Simulants, who have brought guns, as is tradition. The quizmaster is sweating. "Final question, for the engine upgrade," he says, very carefully. "What... is love?"

success.text: The quizmaster bursts into tears. The audience stands. Even the Simulants lower their guns and clap. You win the engine upgrade, and a small trophy shaped like a fish.

fail.text: "That's not an answer, that's a song," says the quizmaster. The Simulants take the prize, and then shoot it, because that's who they are.

choices.text: "A chemical reaction to an evolutionary need to breed."

success.text: The Simulants nod. "Correct," says the quizmaster, coldly. You win the upgrade and the audience's lasting contempt.

fail.text: "Wrong. Also, that's grim." The Simulants take the prize. They're quite moved, actually.

effect.text: You draw first. The Simulants are delighted: finally, a team that understands the spirit of the game.

events.text: {crew} the mechanoid has finally booked their Space Corps driving test. The examiner is a cyborg with a clipboard and no sense of humour. "Three manoeuvres," he says. "One error and you fail. You have failed already for looking nervous."

effect.text: {who} straps in, checks the mirrors forty times and pulls away at walking pace. The examiner makes a note. It's a long note.

success.text: He pockets it without looking up. "Pass," he writes. Then he gets out. The licence is technically valid.

fail.text: He pockets it, writes 'attempted bribery' on the form and stays for the whole test anyway.

effect.text: It's the thirty-ninth time the test has been postponed. The examiner says he'll wait. He has a very long life ahead of him.

events.text: The driving test, part two: the emergency stop. The examiner bangs on the dashboard. Something comes round the corner at the same moment: an asteroid, a Simulant cruiser and an ice-cream van, all at once.

success.text: Perfect stop. The asteroid misses. The cruiser hits the asteroid. The van sells you a 99 with a flake. The examiner gives a tiny nod.

fail.text: A very good stop, right in front of the cruiser. The examiner writes 'did not consider Simulants' and you have to fight your way out.

success.text: You thread between all three at full speed. The examiner has gone white. "That's not an emergency stop," he says faintly, "but I'll allow it."

fail.text: You hit the ice-cream van. There is raspberry sauce on the hull for weeks.

events.text: The final part of the driving test: parallel parking between two Simulant battleships. The examiner looks up from his clipboard. "Take your time," he says. "They're asleep. For now."

success.text: You park it perfectly. The battleships don't wake. The examiner shakes your hand and gives you a licence and a coupon for a free car wash. The whole crew are better pilots for watching.

fail.text: You bump one. Very gently. It wakes up. It's not happy.

choices.text: Skip it and drive off with the clipboard.

effect.text: You drive off with the examiner's clipboard. It holds every test result he's ever written, plus the scrap he's taken in bribes.

events.text: Holly has started talking to the computer of a lonely lighthouse beacon. Late at night. In a voice nobody has heard before. She says it's just "networking". It's been networking for nine hours.

effect.text: The ship's lights dim romantically. Holly hums. You hear the word "bandwidth" whispered in a way that makes everyone uncomfortable.

success.text: It's a sweet conversation, mostly about tide tables and how lonely it is to be the only one awake. Then it isn't sweet at all. You stop listening. You can never unhear it.

fail.text: Holly catches you and shuts down the hot water for a week out of spite.

effect.text: Holly goes very quiet. She doesn't say anything. For the next three jumps, every map she gives you is slightly wrong. On purpose.

events.text: Holly's lighthouse wants to meet in person. Since it is a lighthouse, and Holly is a computer, this means docking the ship to it and plugging the two of them together. Holly asks if anyone has a cable. And candles.

effect.text: You dock with the lighthouse. Holly and the lighthouse plug in. The ship's systems go haywire for an hour, in what everyone politely agrees to call 'a firmware update'.

choices.text: Tell Holly she can do better.

success.text: Holly thinks about it. "You're right," she says. "It only has one light. I deserve at least two." She gives the ship a free sensor upgrade to cheer herself up.

fail.text: Holly takes this very badly. She sulks, and the oxygen goes a bit thin for a day.

events.text: The lighthouse has proposed. To Holly. On the comms, in front of everyone. It's offered a dowry of fuel and a light that never goes out. Holly is looking at you, as much as a face on a screen can look.

effect.text: A brief, beautiful ceremony. The lighthouse flashes 'I DO' in Morse. Holly stays aboard, but now has a long-distance husband she phones every night. The dowry is generous.

success.text: You object. Holly agrees with you, mostly out of relief. The lighthouse takes it well, and gives you some fuel anyway as a goodbye.

fail.text: Holly is furious. "Who asked you?" She marries the lighthouse anyway and doesn't invite you. You weren't invited to your own ship's wedding.

weapons.name: Starbug Laser Cannon
weapons.desc: Starbug's twin cannon. Slow to get going, but it warms up: every shot makes the next one come sooner.

weapons.name: Bazookoid Rack
weapons.desc: Mining bazookoids with a homing chip Kryten fitted. They chase their target round corners. They never miss.

weapons.name: Bazookoid Mk II
weapons.desc: A heavy bazookoid that Kryten tuned up. One shot in four hits twice as hard.

weapons.name: JMC Mining Laser
weapons.desc: Made for cutting asteroids open, and it still sorts the good metal out of whatever it cuts. Every hit salvages scrap.

weapons.name: Simulant Plasma Lance
weapons.desc: Pulled off a dead Simulant ship. It doesn't just burn: it drains the power out of every system it touches.

weapons.name: GELF Harpoon
weapons.desc: A barbed GELF harpoon on a long chain. Once it bites, the target can't dodge for six seconds.

weapons.name: Vindaloo Torpedo
weapons.desc: A torpedo packed with Lister's emergency curry. Sets the room on fire and the fumes leave nobody breathing.

weapons.name: Toaster Ion Lobber
weapons.desc: Fires electrified crumpets. Knocks out a system, and every volley feeds your crew a hot crumpet too.

weapons.name: Rimmer's Scattergun
weapons.desc: Rimmer designed it himself. Four fragments, and nobody, least of all Rimmer, knows how hard each one will hit.

weapons.name: Hex-Field Disruptor
weapons.desc: Kryten built it from a vending machine and a guilt chip. Scrambles systems, stuns the crew, and sends them running from the room.

weapons.name: Ace's Wildfire Cannon
weapons.desc: The cannon from a dashing hero's test ship, left behind in a dimension rip. Three shots, and every one of them might be the one that counts.

weapons.name: Light Bee Projector
weapons.desc: Fires a real shot and a hologram of your ship at the same time. Each volley adds a point of super shield while the enemy works out which ship is real.

weapons.name: Polymorph Canister
weapons.desc: A canister holding a very small, very upset polymorph. It turns into everyone's worst fear. The crew in that room leave. Quickly.

weapons.name: Skutter Rivet Gun
weapons.desc: The skutters built it from a riveting machine. Every hit ricochets into another room.

weapons.name: White Hole Lens
weapons.desc: A lens ground from a white hole's afterglow. Its beam pins time itself: the target can't dodge while it burns.

drones.name: Skutter
drones.desc: A small, long-suffering cleaning robot. Repairs your systems, and makes rude gestures when it thinks nobody is looking.

drones.name: Armed Skutter
drones.desc: A skutter with a laser taped to it. Flies out and shoots at the enemy, very pleased with itself.

drones.name: Light Bee Interceptor
drones.desc: A spare hologram light bee that buzzes about outside and pops incoming missiles.

augments.name: Holly (Backup)
augments.desc: The ship's computer, on a backup drive. Claims an IQ of 6000. Weapons charge 5% faster.

augments.name: Hard-Light Drive
augments.desc: Upgrades your hologram projectors to hard light. Your crew hit 15% harder.

augments.name: Space Corps Directives
augments.desc: Rimmer's dog-eared copy. He reads one out in every crisis. +5% evasion: everyone flies faster to get away from him.

augments.name: Food Dispenser
augments.desc: Your crew heal slowly anywhere. It only makes chicken soup, always on the wrong setting.

augments.name: Kryten's Spare Heads
augments.desc: Three spare heads, each with its own opinions. Crew repair 25% faster.

augments.name: Stasis Booth
augments.desc: Systems hit while the booth is humming are frozen in time, not broken. 15% chance to shrug off system damage.

augments.name: Lister's Guitar
augments.desc: Lister plays it when things get tense. Crew move 15% faster, mainly away from it.

augments.name: Hologrammatic Decoy
augments.desc: Projects a second Starbug next to the first. Starts every fight with a 3-point super shield while the enemy works out which is real.

augments.name: Toaster-Wired Reactor
augments.desc: Talkie Toaster runs the reactor now: weapons charge 15% faster. Every few jumps it vents a room by accident.

augments.name: Unbreakable Delusion
augments.desc: The crew survived the despair squid's ink and came out believing in themselves a bit too much: they heal slowly anywhere on the ship.

augments.name: Mirror Finish
augments.desc: Kryten polished the hull until enemy gunners kept aiming at their own reflection. +7% evasion.

arms.name: Hand Bazookoid
arms.desc: A mining bazookoid, carried by hand. Clears corridors, and the rooms either side of them.

arms.name: Kryten's Spare Arm
arms.desc: Detachable. Still twitches. Makes a decent club and a better spanner.

arms.name: Space Corps Directives (Hardback)
arms.desc: Rimmer reads one out mid-swing. Opponents are stunned, mostly by the directive.

arms.name: Vindaloo Ladle
arms.desc: Still dripping. The smell alone sends boarders running.

arms.name: Hard-Light Overcoat
arms.desc: A hologram trick: blows go straight through it, mostly. Needs no air.

items.name: Lister's Lager
items.desc: Two fights of extra courage and slightly worse walking.

items.name: Cold Chicken Vindaloo
items.desc: Eaten straight from the fridge at four in the morning. Builds character, and muscle.

items.name: Holly's IQ Pills
items.desc: Holly swears they work. They work, a bit.

items.name: Thermonuclear Vindaloo
items.desc: Lister's masterpiece. For the next three fights: +60% hand-to-hand damage and +30% speed. Eyes water at fifty paces.

items.name: Triple Fried-Egg Chilli
items.desc: Lister's breakfast. One fight of fury, then a long sit-down.
